deep.reconstruction:
Context. This folio belongs to Riemann's work on genus p=3: the plane quartic, its 28 bitangents, and their expression by theta constants. The previous page works with Riemann's normal form of the quartic, sqrt(x*xi)+sqrt(y*eta)+sqrt(z*zeta)=0, built from an Aronhold-type set of bitangents with coefficients alpha, beta, gamma. This page expresses those coefficients through theta constants and derives linear and quadratic relations among the bitangent forms.

Notation (my reading of the image). Eight letters label the theta characteristics, chosen as subsets of {r,s,u,v,w,a,b,c}.
- A pair (rs, ab, ru, bc, ...) is one of the C(8,2)=28 odd characteristics. theta'(rs) is the gradient at 0 of the odd theta function, i.e. the corresponding bitangent as a linear form.
- A quadruple is one of the 35 nonzero even characteristics; a quadruple and its complement in the 8 letters are the same characteristic. Together with theta(0) this gives the 36 even characteristics.
- theta(rsab) is the even theta constant.

(1) Top lines. Riemann starts from a general addition/product formula, of the form theta'(b+c) * Prod theta(...) = Sum_a theta'(...) * Prod theta(...). It is visibly a consequence of Riemann's theta formula, differentiated once at 0 so that odd thetas enter through their gradients. He specialises it to
 theta'(bc) theta(0) theta(buvw) theta(cuvw) = Sum_u theta'(ru) theta(rubc) theta(buas) theta(cuas),
with a second version with r and s interchanged. This is a linear relation among bitangent forms (gradients of odd thetas) whose coefficients are cubic monomials in even theta constants. It is the theta-function version of the linear dependencies among bitangents of an Aronhold set.

Beside this is the combination theta'(rs) theta(rsab) theta(rsac) theta(rsbc), the natural normalisation of the bitangent rs. Also a relation
 theta'(rs) theta(uabc) theta(vabc) theta(wabc) = theta'(ab) theta(ursc) theta(vrsc) theta(wrsc).
I read this as a normalisation linking the forms rs and ab, perhaps a single matching coordinate; the image is ambiguous.

(2) Moduli as theta quotients. Riemann sets
- alpha1 = theta(rubc)/theta(subc)
- beta1 = theta(ruac)/theta(suac)
- gamma1 = theta(ruab)/theta(suab)
- delta1 = alpha1*beta1*gamma1
He writes the quotients beta1/alpha1, gamma1/alpha1 and delta1/alpha1 as fourfold theta quotients. For example delta1/alpha1 = theta(ruab) theta(ruac)/(theta(suab) theta(suac)), consistent with delta1 = alpha1*beta1*gamma1. These are the Riemann–Weber expressions of the quartic's coefficients through theta constants. The next page repeats them as alpha, beta, gamma, delta = alpha*beta*gamma, with primed versions for v in place of u.

(3) Normalising factors.
- mu_a = theta(ursa) theta(vrsa) theta(wrsa)/(theta_0 theta(buvw) theta(cuvw)).
- mu_theta = theta(uabc) theta(vabc) theta(wabc)/(theta(auvw) theta(buvw) theta(cuvw)).
- a = theta(ursa) theta(vrsa) theta(wrsa) theta(rsbc) = theta(vwbc) theta(uwbc) theta(uvbc) theta(uvwa). This equality is only the rewriting of each quadruple as its complement.
- 'theta' = theta(uabc) theta(vabc) theta(wabc) theta(0).

(4) Table of the 28 bitangents in a second 8-letter labelling {p,q,r,s,a,b,c,u}:
- pq pr ps / rs qs qr: 6 pairs inside {p,q,r,s};
- ap..as, bp..bs, cp..cs, up..us: 16 mixed pairs;
- the remaining 6 pairs come from {a,b,c,u}.
The correspondence 'vw pqrs = uabc' links the two labellings: a characteristic written with v,w in one equals uabc in the other. Riemann then assigns to bitangents coordinate-type values a, b, c, 1/a, 1/b, 1/c. He records b/c = alpha2*alpha3, c/a = alpha2'*alpha3', a/b = alpha2''*alpha3''. He then gives rows like (1/(alpha2'alpha3'), alpha2*alpha3, 1). These are coefficient vectors of bitangents in coordinates of the type (x, 1/y, 1); compare the 3x3 determinants a^{23}, a_{23} on the next page.

Alongside are lists of products of pairs of bitangents such as pvr.qws, qvr.pws, pvs.qwr, vpq.wrs, vpr.wqs, vps.wqr. These are the quadratic (product) expressions, i.e. the conics through the contact points, from which the quartic is written as a combination of products of bitangent forms.

(5) Middle-left. With (alpha gamma delta), (beta gamma delta) denoting 3x3 determinants of bitangent coefficients and primes the second system, Riemann writes two proportionalities with a common factor lambda. He eliminates lambda by multiplying and dividing, getting (beta3^+/alpha3^+)^2 = (alpha gamma delta)/(alpha gamma delta)' * (beta gamma delta)'/(beta gamma delta). He also gets a square formula for the product. Then come entries like (1/(alpha2'^2 alpha3'^2)) (beta gamma delta)/(beta gamma delta)', alpha2^2 alpha3^2 (beta gamma delta)/(beta gamma delta)', and so on.

(6) Bottom. Squares of normalising constants of bitangent triples, e.g.
(upq)^2 = a^{12} a_{23} a^{13}/(a_{12} a^{23} a_{13} alpha1'^2) = a_3^1 a^{13}/(a_1^3 a_{13} alpha1'^2) = 1/alpha1,
where a^{ij}, a_{ij}, a_i^j are the determinants defined on the next page. He also writes (pqu)^2 = alpha1'^2/alpha1 and (psq)^2 = 1/alpha1, and a list 1/alpha1, ..., 1/(alpha1' alpha1), alpha1'^2/alpha1 for pqu, psu, qsu. The intermediate equalities use determinant identities proved on the next page (e.g. a_2^1 a_3^2 a_1^3 = a_1^2 a_3^1 a_2^3). I cannot verify them from this page alone.

Purpose. To express the coefficients of Riemann's normal form of the plane quartic, and the normalisations of all 28 bitangents, through even theta constants and gradients of odd theta functions. This is the material of Riemann's p=3 theory, as published posthumously and worked out in Weber's 1876 monograph.
errors: No definite mathematical error is visible. The quotients beta1/alpha1, gamma1/alpha1 and delta1/alpha1 are consistent with the definitions of alpha1, beta1, gamma1 and with delta1 = alpha1*beta1*gamma1.

The lambda-elimination in the middle-left block is compressed. Depending on how the superscripts (alpha3^+ vs beta3^+) are read, the stated squared ratio follows only if the two proportionalities have reciprocal right-hand sides. This cannot be confirmed from the image.
The chain (upq)^2 = ... = 1/alpha1 relies on determinant identities established on the next page. It is unchecked here.

The relation theta'(rs) theta(uabc) theta(vabc) theta(wabc) = theta'(ab) theta(ursc) theta(vrsc) theta(wrsc) equates gradient vectors of two different odd characteristics up to scalars. As a vector identity it cannot hold literally. It must mean a normalisation, e.g. one matching coordinate, or it is a working shorthand.

results.what: Linear relations among gradients theta'(odd) at 0 with coefficients products of three even theta constants, obtained from Riemann's theta formula
results.modern_name: Linear relations among bitangents of a plane quartic via odd theta gradients (theta-formula consequences)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (p=3 paper, published posthumously 1876) and H. Weber 1876

results.what: alpha = theta(rubc)/theta(subc), beta = theta(ruac)/theta(suac), gamma = theta(ruab)/theta(suab), delta = alpha*beta*gamma as moduli of the quartic
results.modern_name: Riemann–Weber formulas for the Riemann model of a plane quartic (Weber's formula)

results.what: Labelling of 28 odd and 36 even genus-3 characteristics by pairs and quadruple-pairs of 8 letters, and conversion between two such labellings
results.modern_name: Aronhold/Cayley–Hesse 8-letter notation for bitangents; Steiner complexes
results.usually_credited_to: Hesse, Cayley, Aronhold (1850s); theta version Riemann/Weber

results.what: Normalisation constants of bitangent triples (e.g. (upq)^2 = 1/alpha1) via 3x3 determinants of bitangent coefficient vectors
results.modern_name: Reconstruction of the 28 bitangents from an Aronhold set (Riemann's construction)

deep.surprise_reason: This is working material for Riemann's own genus-3 theory: theta-quotient moduli, bitangent labelling and linear/quadratic bitangent relations. That theory is published posthumously in his Werke and in Weber's 1876 monograph explicitly derived from Riemann. Nothing here appears to anticipate a result credited to someone later.
